- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average of history, adjust forecast toward historical mean (not latest peak or trough).
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.53, 0.10, 0.53), model tends to misalign with true trend; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5 days for bias correction.
